cues: Some in positive sentences and in offers: would you like some tea?
Any in negatives and questions, or meaning it doesn't matter which: take any seat.
Each and every both take a singular noun and verb; each looks at members one by one, every at the whole group.
Either, neither and both are for two; all for more than two.
And fewer counts while less measures: fewer students, less sugar.
